title: 第58章 方少躬身，谁才是规矩？

第58章 方少躬身，谁才是规矩？-《重生2000：撕了协议我暴富了》

“没听说过。怎么，这人惹到你了？”

顾城的声音从手机听筒里传出来，不大，但包间里安静得掉根针都能听见。

周斌搭在扶手上的手指微微蜷了一下，笑还挂着，但眼皮跳了一下。

林川端着酒杯，没看他。

“没什么大事，在成都陪我女朋友家里人吃饭，碰上一个不太长眼的。”

电话那头顿了一秒。

“哪个酒店？”

“锦江香格里拉，三楼中餐厅，锦绣厅。”

“行，你先吃着。等十来分钟。”

电话挂了。

林川把手机搁回桌面，拿起筷子，夹了一块和牛放进沈蔓碗里。

“多吃点，这个五分熟的刚好。”

全程没再看周斌一眼。

周斌坐在那把自己拽来的椅子上，两条腿的二郎腿已经放下来了。

嘴上还撑着，但声调比刚才矮了半截。

“打个电话就能吓着谁？成都又不是上海，你在那边认识几个人，到了这儿不一定好使。”

他说这话的时候，右手无意识地摸了一下裤兜里的车钥匙。

林川没接。

沈蔓坐在副位上，筷子搁在碗边，转头看着周斌。

“周斌，你走吧。”

“我走？”周斌愣了一下，随即往椅背上一靠，“蔓蔓，咱们高中同学，我就是来打个招呼，怎么了？你这男朋友脾气也太大了吧——”

“我让你走。”

沈蔓的声音不高，但每个字都咬得清楚。

周斌看了她两秒，又扫了一眼对面的沈母和大伯夫妇，嘴角勾了一下。

“我今天倒要看看，你这位上海来的男朋友，能在成都叫来什么人。还有沈蔓，你别被人骗了。”

他说完这句话，往后一仰，双臂抱在胸前，摆出一副看戏的姿态。

包间里的气氛很难形容。

大伯母坐在角落，两只手规规矩矩地叠在膝盖上，瓜子早就不嗑了。

大伯端着茶杯，杯沿贴着嘴唇，一口都没喝进去。

沈母低着头，视线落在桌面上，筷子一动没动。

没人说话。

林川叫了服务员进来。

“后面的菜上一下，再给这边添碗松茸汤。”

服务员应了一声，转身出去了。

周斌坐在那儿，翘着的二郎腿又放下了，又翘起来，又放下。

他从兜里掏出手机看了一眼，没有新消息。犹豫了两秒，打开通讯录翻了翻，找到一个名字，拇指悬在拨号键上方——最后还是退了出去。

他想打电话叫人。

但叫谁？叫过来干什么？他在成都认识的那些人，最大的不过是几个工地老板和建材市场的同行，撑死了一个区商会的副秘书长。

林川给沈母舀了一碗汤端过去。

“阿姨，松茸汤趁热喝。”

沈母接过碗，手抖了一下，汤差点洒出来。

“好好好，谢谢。”

又过了大概五六分钟。

窗外突然传来一阵密集的引擎声。

不是一辆车。

是很多辆。

声浪压过了街面上所有的背景噪音，低沉、浑厚，带着大排量发动机特有的共振。

"Never heard of it. Why, did this person offend you?"

Gu Cheng's voice came from the receiver of the mobile phone. It was not loud, but it was so quiet in the private room that you could hear a pin drop.

Zhou Bin's fingers on the armrest curled up slightly, his smile still hanging on his face, but his eyelids twitched.

Lin Chuan held the wine glass without looking at him.

"It's nothing serious. I was having dinner with my girlfriend's family in Chengdu, and I met someone who wasn't very discerning."

The other end of the phone paused for a second.

"Which hotel?"

"Jinjiang Shangri-La, Chinese restaurant on the third floor, Jinxiu Hall."

"Okay, you eat first. Wait about ten minutes."

The phone was hung up.

Lin Chuan put the phone back on the table, picked up the chopsticks, picked up a piece of wagyu and put it into Shen Man's bowl.

"Eat more, this medium rare is just right."

He didn’t look at Zhou Bin again during the whole process.

Zhou Bin sat on the chair he had pulled over, his legs already down.

His mouth was still open, but his tone was half lower than before.

"Who can be scared by just making a phone call? Chengdu is not Shanghai. If you know a few people there, it may not be easy for you here."

When he said this, his right hand unconsciously touched the car key in his trouser pocket.

Lin Chuan didn't answer.

Shen Man sat on the deputy seat, put her chopsticks on the edge of the bowl, and turned to look at Zhou Bin.

"Zhou Bin, let's go."

"Should I leave?" Zhou Bin was stunned for a moment, then leaned back in his chair, "Manman, we are classmates in high school, and I just came to say hello. What's wrong? Your boyfriend has a bad temper, right?"

"I let you go."

Shen Man's voice was not high, but every word was pronounced clearly.

Zhou Bin looked at her for two seconds, then glanced at Mother Shen and Uncle Shen opposite him, and the corners of his mouth curled up.

"I want to see who your boyfriend from Shanghai can call in Chengdu today. And Shen Man, don't be deceived."

After he said this, he leaned back, folded his arms in front of his chest, and assumed a show-watching posture.

The atmosphere in the private room is hard to describe.

The eldest aunt was sitting in the corner, her hands folded neatly on her knees, and she had stopped eating melon seeds for a long time.

The uncle held the tea cup, the rim of the cup was close to his lips, and he didn't take a sip.

Mother Shen lowered her head, her eyes fell on the table, and her chopsticks did not move.

No one spoke.

Lin Chuan called the waiter to come in.

"Let's serve the dishes later and add a bowl of matsutake soup here."

The waiter responded, turned around and went out.

Zhou Bin sat there with his crossed legs lowered, raised, and lowered again.

He took his cell phone out of his pocket and looked at it. There was no new message.After hesitating for two seconds, he opened the address book, flipped through it, found a name, and hovered his thumb over the dial key—and finally backed out.

He wanted to call someone.

But who?Why did you call me here?The biggest people he knew in Chengdu were just a few construction site bosses and colleagues in the building materials market, and they defeated the deputy secretary-general of a district chamber of commerce.

Lin Chuan scooped up a bowl of soup for Mother Shen and brought it over.

"Auntie, drink the matsutake soup while it's hot."

Mother Shen took the bowl, her hands shook and the soup almost spilled.

"Okay, okay, thank you."

About five or six minutes passed.

Suddenly there was a heavy sound of engines outside the window.

Not a car.

It's a lot of cars.

The sound waves overwhelmed all the background noise on the street. It was low and thick, with the unique resonance of a large-displacement engine.
